row.scim_plan: Pro Suite + Web Services API add-on
row.scim_price_text: Pro Suite $100/u/mo + Web Services API $25/u/mo (API included from Core, $195/u/mo)
row.scim_addon_price_text: Web Services API: $25/u/mo on Pro Suite
row.evidence: Salesforce's SCIM is a REST API that needs an OAuth token, and Salesforce API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer orgs while Professional Edition orgs add it as an add-on; the Sales pricing page lists Web Services API at 'Additional $25 USD/user/month' on Pro Suite and not on Starter Suite.
row.notes: Changed since June: the Sales Cloud pricing page no longer lists Enterprise ($175); the line-up is now Free Suite $0, Starter Suite $25, Pro Suite $100, Core $195, Advanced $395, Max $550 (annual). Core is described as 'Everything in Professional Edition plus Momentum and Premier Success'. SCIM help pages say 'Available in: All Editions', but SCIM is a REST API and API access is off on Starter, an add-on ($25/u/mo) on Pro Suite and included from Core, so the SCIM plan is recorded as Pro Suite + API add-on ($125/u/mo, 5x Starter). The June 'Enterprise $175' price and the '~6% price rise' claim were not found on a first-party page and are dropped. SAML federated SSO is in all editions. SCIM DELETE deactivates (never deletes); group create is not supported. Entra provisions through Salesforce's API rather than SCIM.

plans.name: Free Suite
plans.notes: SAML federated authentication is in all editions. SCIM help pages say 'All Editions', but SCIM is a REST API and this suite has no Web Services API (see conflicts).

plans.name: Starter Suite
plans.notes: Web Services API not included on Starter Suite; SCIM availability on this suite is therefore unclear (see conflicts).

plans.name: Pro Suite
plans.notes: Web Services API is an add-on at $25 USD/user/month (Professional Edition API add-on).

scim.plan: Pro Suite + Web Services API add-on
scim.addon_price_text: Web Services API: Additional $25 USD/user/month on Pro Suite (included from Core)
scim.notes: SCIM help pages say 'Available in: All Editions', but SCIM is driven through REST API calls with an OAuth token, and Salesforce API access is only on Enterprise-class editions or as a Professional Edition add-on. Plan gate is inferred from the API gate; Salesforce does not say in one place that SCIM needs API access. sso_required false: Salesforce docs do not require SSO; Google's own page requires SSO for its connector.

endpoints.notes: Also /Entitlements (profiles and permission sets) and /Roles, read-only. The reference sheet spells the endpoint ServiceProviderConfigs (plural).

operations.notes: DELETE on /Users deactivates, it does not delete. Groups support only GET and PATCH (membership), not create; PUT is not listed.

deprovision.data_retained: User object is kept and can still be queried with active=false; user cannot log in; can be reactivated with PATCH active=true.

filtering.notes: Filter supported (maxResults 200); attribute names and operators are case-sensitive; entitlements and groups (Users) and members (Groups, Entitlements) must be filtered on their own. Full filterable attribute list not documented.

pagination.notes: Lists return a maximum of 200 results; docs show GET /Groups/* to override the 200 limit. startIndex/count paging is not described.

custom.how: Custom User fields under urn:salesforce:schemas:extension:18CHARORGID. Salesforce extension urn:salesforce:schemas:extension:2.0 adds alias, callCenterId, extension (phone extension); urn:salesforce:schemas:extension:external:2.0 adds accountId, contactId, community; urn:salesforce:schemas:extension:communities adds networkID, networkName.

roles.how: UserRoleId maps to the SCIM roles attribute (PATCH to update a user's role, /Roles readable); profiles and permission sets assigned via the entitlements attribute.

limitations.text: Only one phone number per user can be set through SCIM.
Bulk not supported; sort and etag unsupported per ServiceProviderConfig.
Groups (public groups) cannot be created through SCIM, only read and their membership patched.

user_api.plan: Pro Suite (Web Services API add-on, $25/user/month); included from Core
user_api.notes: Salesforce also offers SOAP, Bulk and other APIs; only the REST sObject resources used for the User object are recorded here.

capabilities.notes: User is a standard sObject; deactivate and reactivate shown via SCIM (same REST API family). Generic sObject DELETE exists but deleting users is not documented.

endpoints.purpose: Create a record (sObject=User to create a user)

limitations.text: Orgs without API access get API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG; every API user needs the API Enabled permission.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SWA, SCIM and Create/Update/Deactivate/Sync Password/Schema Discovery/Attribute Writeback as checked (read from page markup); Group Push not checked.

entra.notes: Entra provisions through Salesforce's user account provisioning API (v40) with username, password and security token, not SCIM.

google.notes: Google's page does not say whether its connector uses SCIM or Salesforce's REST API.

conflicts.text: Salesforce's SCIM help pages say SCIM is 'Available in: All Editions', but SCIM is driven by REST API calls and the REST API guide and Sales pricing page put API access only on Enterprise-class editions / Core and above, or as a $25/user/month add-on on Professional / Pro Suite (not on Starter Suite).

open_questions: Salesforce does not state in one place whether SCIM works on editions without API access (Starter Suite, Pro Suite without the API add-on).
Whether SCIM deactivation frees the license or revokes active sessions is not documented on the SCIM pages.
SCIM token setup (connected app / external client app) and token lifetime are not described on the SCIM pages.
Audit-log API (Setup Audit Trail, Event Monitoring) and user-event webhooks were not researched to a first-party citation.
OneLogin connector not checked (OneLogin pages block bots); no Salesforce-hosted OneLogin guide found.
Whether Google Workspace's Salesforce connector uses SCIM or Salesforce's REST API.
API rate limits for SCIM are not documented on the SCIM pages.
